type.description: Select capabilities. gui is native desktop; browser is HTML; server exposes routes. tui is an interactive terminal interface. Only one of these four renderers is allowed; add terminal/database alongside it.

title.description: Set the desktop window or browser page title.

port.description: Choose an HTTP port, 0–65535. Zero asks the operating system for a free port.

host.description: Set the HTTP bind interface. Loopback is the default; 0.0.0.0 exposes interfaces but does not bypass allowed_hosts.

http_settings.description: Configure validated transport/security limits, host/CORS policies, bearer authentication, access logging and request execution budgets. See the HTTP deployment guide for every setting.

debugging.description: Enable log debug messages in the terminal. off suppresses them. say output is independent.

window_style.description: Set shared inherited widget styling and the desktop/page background.

window_size.description: Set the native desktop window dimensions, each 100–4096 pixels. Browser viewport size remains controlled by the browser.

layout.description: Stack widgets vertically (default), horizontally, or use layout is grid 4 columns (1–12 columns). Grid supports column_span styling and preserves declaration order. Available since 0.4.0.

panel.description: Declare a named grouping container for GUI/browser widgets. Use place to assign children; panels may nest without cycles. Default layout is vertical.

place.description: Assign a widget to a panel, independent of declaration order. Root declaration; only one parent per widget. GUI/browser only.

panel_layout.description: Set a panel layout: vertical, horizontal, or grid 1–12 columns. Other panels keep their own layout.

theme.description: Choose light or dark built-in palettes. Sets semantic tokens background/surface/text/muted/primary/danger/border and sensible widget defaults. Root declaration.

design_tokens.description: Declare or override semantic tokens before styles resolve. Reference with "$primary" in style records. Values validate at use; theme/tokens work regardless of declaration order.

motion.description: Disable browser and native animations for this app. Browser additionally honors prefers-reduced-motion. Root declaration; on is default.

assets.description: Serve allowlisted local images/fonts at /__ucl/assets/NAME for browser CSS. Directory is relative to source; traversal, outside symlinks, executable formats, and oversized files are rejected. Authentication/host/rate policies still apply.

stylesheet.description: Load trusted local compiled CSS for browser apps, relative to the UCL source file (8 MiB limit). Supports compiled Tailwind of any version. No CDN or Node runtime needed. See design guide.

classes.description: Set browser utility classes. Build CSS with ucl design or your own Tailwind pipeline; runtime never fetches remote CSS. Record styles and utilities coexist; helper uses important utilities.

state_style.description: Style hover/focus/active/disabled states in GUI or browser. Native bindings update immediately; browser uses CSS pseudo-classes. No TUI hover states.

responsive_style.description: Browser-only min-width variant: sm 640, md 768, lg 1024, xl 1280, 2xl 1536 pixels. Named breakpoints have deterministic ascending cascade.

animate.description: Animate native numeric/#RRGGBB style values with cancellable Tk callbacks, or emit browser keyframes from current to target style. Duration 0–60000 ms. No TUI animations. Browser is server-rendered: animation plays on the next response, not live DOM updates.

close_interface.description: Close a native GUI or end a TUI input loop. Browser/server shutdown is not exposed to click handlers.

widget_style.description: Set or update validated styles for any widget. Properties: color, background, font_size, font_weight, padding, margin, width, align, border_width, column_span. Can appear before the root widget declaration.

label_named.description: Declare an addressable live text label. show text "0" is #counter is an alias. Requires gui or browser.

input.description: Declare a single-line text input with the given caption. Starts empty. Requires gui or browser.

checkbox.description: Declare a boolean checkbox, initially false. Use read input and input value updates to interact with it.

label_update.description: Replace a label value immediately in desktop mode or on the next browser render.

input_update.description: Set input text or a checkbox boolean. Updates the native widget and shared browser model.

focus_input.description: Focus a native text input, optionally selecting its contents for replacement. Omit selecting all to place the cursor at the end. Available since 0.4.0; requires gui.

read_input.description: Read input text or checkbox boolean into a sequential variable. Browser forms submit their fields before the click handler executes.

widget_state.description: enable/disable controls interaction; hide/reveal controls visibility. Applies to any widget; hidden/disabled browser buttons are also rejected server-side.

close_window.description: Close an open native desktop window from a handler/timer and end its event loop. Timers are not rescheduled after closure. Not available in browser mode.

timer.description: Run a native GUI callback periodically (10–86400000 ms). A failing callback logs an error and stops that timer. Browser timers are not implemented.

ask_text.description: Read terminal text. ask for secret hides entered text using the terminal password reader. Not available in GUI/HTTP handlers, to avoid blocking event loops.

log.description: Emit debug/info/warning/error diagnostics to stderr; --log-format json and --log-file also apply. GUI applications retain their console; use say alongside GUI updates.

while.syntax: while count < 10 [ set count to count + 1 ]
while.description: Execute a block while its condition is truthy. HTTP execution budgets also count empty loop iterations.

for.syntax: for each name in list("Ada", "Lin") [ say name ]
for.description: Iterate list/tuple/range/string values or record keys, assigning the iteration variable.

break.description: Exit the innermost loop; only valid inside a loop in the same function/handler.

continue.description: Skip to the next iteration of the innermost loop.

try.description: Execute a block and capture UCL runtime failures for an immediately following catch. Execution budget exhaustion cannot be caught.

catch.description: Handle the preceding try failure; error receives its diagnostic text. Skipped when no failure occurred.

assert.description: Raise a UCL runtime error if the expression is false. Can be handled with try/catch.

read_file.description: Read a UTF-8 text file into a sequential variable. Paths are relative to the process working directory; no implicit sandbox.

write_file.description: Write UTF-8 text, replacing the file. append "more" to file "notes.txt" appends instead. Parent directories must exist.

append.description: Append a value to an existing list variable. Mutates the list, including shared object properties that reference that list.

respond_typed.description: End a route with text/plain. respond html returns trusted text/html; escape untrusted data yourself. Default respond serializes JSON.

header.description: Set a printable ASCII response header. CR/LF and transport-owned headers are rejected. Requires a route.

require.description: If false, end the route with a generic JSON rejection and a 400–599 status. Place outside transaction blocks.

transaction.syntax: transaction on app [ execute "INSERT INTO notes VALUES (?)" on app using list("hi") ]
transaction.description: Run a block in one SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, committing on success and rolling back on failure. Nested transactions on the same connection are rejected. Respond after the block.

property.description: Update an already-declared record/object property, including nested properties.

create.description: Deep-copy an object template into an independent instance. Root instances initialize before actions; local instances initialize sequentially.

let.description: Declare a value (be/is/to accepted). Root let declarations dependency-resolve before actions. set count to 1 updates an existing value sequentially. Function/route scalar environments are local copies.

ask_number.description: Read an integer or finite decimal from the terminal, retrying invalid input. EOF is a UCL error; Ctrl+C cancels. Use subsequent actions, not root initializers, to consume input.

print.description: Write a value to terminal stdout, in any application mode. print is an alias; this never changes GUI text implicitly.

function.description: Declare a function or object method with named parameters. Registered before root actions. Methods receive self; scalar locals do not implicitly mutate global scalars.

call.description: Call a function/method and discard the result. Function/method calls can also appear in expressions.

return.description: End the current function or method, returning a value. Without return the result is nothing.

otherwise.description: Execute the alternative block only when the immediately preceding if was false.

repeat.description: Run a block a nonnegative integer number of times.

object.description: Declare a property/method object template. Properties dependency-resolve; templates are usable instances as well as clone sources.

route.description: Declare an HTTP route. Supports get/post/put/delete/patch, named path parameters, exact-path precedence, HEAD fallback and automatic OPTIONS. Duplicate/ambiguous shapes are rejected.

respond.description: End the route with JSON and the selected status/headers. Missing explicit response is JSON null. JSON cannot contain nonfinite numbers.

status.description: Set a route response status, 200–599. HEAD, 204, 205 and 304 suppress response bodies as required.

database.description: Open a SQLite connection before actions. :memory: is ephemeral; relative paths resolve against the working directory. Connections close on shutdown.

execute.syntax: execute "INSERT INTO users VALUES (?)" on app using list("Ada")
execute.description: Run one parameterized SQL statement. using is optional. Autocommits per statement unless inside a transaction block.

query.syntax: query "SELECT name FROM users" on app into users
query.description: Run SQL returning rows as a list of property records. Optional using binds parameters. Statements without row results are rejected.

buttons.description: Declare one or multiple buttons. Single-button form: show button "Save" is #save. Counts must match; widget IDs are unique across the UI.

style.description: Backward-compatible shorthand for a button background and padding. Prefer style #save is {...} for richer styling.

click.description: Register a desktop/browser click handler. May precede the button declaration. Browser handlers run on the server with submitted input values.

label.description: Declare static text without an ID. Use show label EXPR is #id for later updates.

text.description: Update an existing button caption in either renderer.

builtins.integer: integer(value): integer conversion, truncating numeric values toward zero.
builtins.list: list(a, b, ...): create a list; [] always means a block.
builtins.item: item(collection, key): access a list element, character or record field.
builtins.round: round(number, digits=0): round a number; pass digits positionally.
builtins.json: json(value): serialize a value to a JSON string.
builtins.parse_json: parse_json(text): parse JSON into UCL values.
builtins.environment: environment(name, default=""): read a process environment variable (never log secrets).
builtins.argument: argument(index): get a zero-based CLI --arg value.
builtins.split: split(text, separator): split a string; omit separator for whitespace.
builtins.join: join(values, separator=""): join values as strings.
builtins.range: range(stop) or range(start, stop, step): lazy integer range.
builtins.type_of: type_of(value): runtime type name; object templates use UCLObject.
builtins.sqrt: sqrt(number): square root; negative arguments raise an error.
builtins.escape_html: escape_html(text): escape HTML special characters before interpolating untrusted content into a trusted HTML response.
